cues.text: Welcome to Redox and Electrochemistry.
This recorded Chemistry class uses an AI generated Marin voice.
Oxidation raises oxidation number, while reduction lowers it.
The oxidizing agent accepts electrons and is itself reduced.
The reducing agent supplies electrons and is itself oxidized.
No oxygen atom is required for a redox reaction: zinc can transfer electrons
directly to copper ions.
Oxidation numbers sum to the overall species charge.
An element in its elemental form has oxidation number zero.
Oxygen is usually minus two, but in a peroxide it is minus one.
Hydrogen is usually plus one, but in metal hydrides it is minus one.
Fluorine in its compounds is minus one.
For permanganate, four oxygens contribute minus eight, and the ion's total
charge is minus one.
Manganese must therefore be plus seven.
Reduction to manganese two plus requires five electrons per manganese.
Reduction to manganese dioxide instead ends at plus four and requires three.
The final product fixes the electron count.
In a balanced redox equation, electrons lost equal electrons gained.
Assign oxidation numbers first, identify the two changes, and then use
electron
balance to establish the stoichiometric ratio.
To balance redox half reactions in acidic medium, balance the main element,
oxygen with water, hydrogen with hydrogen ions, and charge with electrons.
For permanganate becoming manganese two plus, place four waters on the product
side, eight hydrogen ions on the reactant side, and five electrons on the
reactant side.
Iron two plus loses one electron to form iron three plus.
Multiply its half reaction by five and add.
The combined equation consumes one permanganate, eight hydrogen ions and five
iron two plus ions.
It produces one manganese two plus, four waters and five iron three plus ions.
Both sides have total charge plus seventeen.
Thus zero point zero two zero zero moles of permanganate require zero point
one
zero zero moles of iron two plus.
In basic medium with manganese dioxide as the specified product, the balanced
reduction consumes one permanganate, two waters and three electrons, forming
one manganese dioxide and four hydroxide ions.
Each side has one manganese, six oxygen and four hydrogen atoms, with charge
minus four.
Zero point zero two zero zero moles now require zero point zero six zero zero
moles of electrons.
Do not copy the acidic five electron count into a reaction with a different
product.
Conductance is the reciprocal of resistance.
Conductivity removes the effect of sample geometry: multiply conductance by
the
cell constant, which is electrode separation divided by area.
Molar conductivity compares conductivity with molar concentration.
With conductivity in siemens per centimetre and concentration in moles per
litre, molar conductivity is one thousand times conductivity divided by
concentration, in siemens centimetres squared per mole.
The factor one thousand comes from the volume unit conversion.
Consider resistance two hundred ohms, cell constant one point two zero per
centimetre, and concentration zero point zero five zero zero molar.
Conductance is zero point zero zero five zero zero siemens.
Conductivity is zero point zero zero six zero zero siemens per centimetre.
Molar conductivity is one hundred twenty siemens centimetres squared per mole.
On dilution, conductivity usually falls because a unit volume contains fewer
ions, while molar conductivity rises as interionic effects decrease and, for
weak electrolytes, ionization increases.
These trends refer to different quantities and are not contradictory.
At infinite dilution, Kohlrausch's law adds the limiting ionic contributions
with their stoichiometric coefficients.
A salt releasing two identical anions contributes that anion term twice.
Always write the units before using a numerical conductivity formula.
A galvanic cell separates oxidation and reduction so electrons can pass
through
an external circuit.
In a Daniell cell, zinc loses electrons at the anode, and copper ions gain
them
at the cathode.
Electrons flow through the wire from zinc to copper.
The salt bridge carries ions that maintain charge balance; electrons do not
travel through its solution.
Anode means oxidation and cathode means reduction in both galvanic and
electrolytic cells.
In a functioning galvanic cell the anode is negative and cathode positive.
An external power supply drives an electrolytic cell, whose electrode
polarities differ, but those reaction based definitions remain.
Cell notation conventionally places the anode on the left and cathode on the
right.
A single line marks a phase boundary, while a double line represents the
electrolyte junction.
Standard reduction potentials are measured relative to a reference electrode,
conventionally the standard hydrogen electrode.
A single isolated electrode potential is not measured without a comparison.
Before calculating voltage, write the oxidation and reduction processes and
balance their electrons.
A correct subtraction formula cannot rescue a reaction whose anode and cathode
were assigned inconsistently.
Using standard reduction potentials, the standard cell voltage equals the
cathode potential minus the anode potential.
Copper two plus to copper has the illustrative value plus zero point three
four
volts, while zinc two plus to zinc has minus zero point seven six.
Their difference is plus one point one zero volts.
Do not multiply electrode potentials when multiplying half reactions to
balance
electrons.
Voltage is an intensive quantity.
Gibbs energy change for the balanced reaction equals minus n times Faraday's
constant times reversible cell voltage.
Here n is two.
With Faraday's constant approximately ninety six thousand five hundred
coulombs
per mole, the standard Gibbs energy change is minus two hundred twelve point
three kilojoules per mole of reaction as written.
Doubling the entire reaction doubles n and the Gibbs energy change, while
leaving voltage unchanged.
Combining this relationship with standard Gibbs energy equals minus R T times
natural log K gives natural log K equals n F times standard voltage divided by
R T.
A positive standard cell voltage therefore implies K greater than one.
At reaction equilibrium the actual voltage is zero, while the standard voltage
need not be zero.
Keep the standard state separate from the present composition.
The Nernst equation corrects the standard voltage for the current mixture.
Cell voltage equals standard voltage minus R T divided by n F, multiplied by
the natural logarithm of the reaction quotient Q.
For a base ten logarithm at approximately two hundred ninety eight kelvin, the
coefficient is about zero point zero five nine one six volts divided by n.
For zinc reacting with copper two plus, Q is approximately zinc ion
concentration divided by copper ion concentration in the ideal dilute model.
Pure solid metals are omitted.
With zinc ions at zero point one zero molar and copper ions at one point zero
molar, Q is zero point one zero.
Its logarithm is minus one.
With n equal to two and standard voltage one point one zero volts, subtracting
the negative correction gives approximately one point one three volts.
In the opposite concentration ratio, Q equal to ten lowers the voltage to
about
one point zero seven volts.
Use dimensionless activities for the rigorous expression, and the stated ideal
approximation for these examples.
At equilibrium, Q equals K and actual reversible voltage is zero.
A concentration cell can have zero standard voltage but a nonzero actual
voltage because its two sides have different activities.
Electrolysis calculations begin with charge, not voltage.
Charge passed is current times time in seconds.
Divide by Faraday's constant to obtain moles of electrons.
Divide again by the electrons required per product particle, then multiply by
molar mass.
Copper two plus requires two electrons to produce one copper atom.
Suppose two point zero zero amperes flow for four thousand eight hundred
twenty
five seconds.
The charge is nine thousand six hundred fifty coulombs.
With Faraday's constant ninety six thousand five hundred coulombs per mole,
this supplies zero point one zero zero moles of electrons and can form zero
point zero five zero zero moles of copper.
Using molar mass sixty three point five grams per mole gives three point one
seven five grams, or three point one eight grams to three significant figures.
That assumes all current produces the desired copper.
At eighty percent current efficiency, multiply by zero point eight zero zero
to
obtain two point five four grams.
Do not divide by the efficiency.
Competing reactions reduce the desired yield for a given charge.
When several cells carry the same charge, each product amount still depends on
its own electron requirement and molar mass.
A primary cell is not designed for normal repeated recharging.
The familiar zinc carbon dry cell uses zinc oxidation and manganese dioxide
cathode chemistry.
Secondary cells are designed for recharging by driving the net chemistry in
reverse.
During lead acid battery discharge, lead is oxidized at the negative electrode
and lead dioxide is reduced at the positive electrode.
Both form lead sulfate.
The net reaction consumes lead, lead dioxide and two sulfuric acid units,
producing two lead sulfate units and two waters.
Acid is consumed during discharge.
The fact that both electrodes form the same sulfate does not mean both were
oxidized: lead changes from zero to plus two, while lead in lead dioxide
changes from plus four to plus two.
Charging reverses the net chemistry with an external energy supply.
A hydrogen oxygen fuel cell receives reactants continuously from outside and
produces water overall.
Two hydrogen molecules combine with one oxygen molecule to form two waters.
Continued operation requires fuel, oxidant and appropriate operating
conditions; it is not unlimited energy.
Distinguish the storage of reactants inside a battery from their external
supply to a fuel cell.
Detailed dry cell mechanisms and electrode classifications remain for further
study.
Conductivity can also estimate how much a weak electrolyte ionizes in a
suitable dilute model.
Divide measured molar conductivity by its limiting molar conductivity to
estimate the ionization fraction alpha.
Suppose a monoprotic acid has molar conductivity twenty and limiting molar
conductivity four hundred, in the same units.
The fraction is zero point zero five zero zero, or five percent.
For starting concentration zero point zero one zero zero molar, the acid
constant is approximately concentration times alpha squared divided by one
minus alpha.
Substitution gives about two point six three times ten to the minus five in
the
conventional concentration model.
Retaining the denominator accounts for the undissociated fraction.
Limiting conductivity may be assembled from limiting ionic contributions using
Kohlrausch's law when direct extrapolation for a weak electrolyte is
unreliable.
This estimate assumes the conductivity ratio is an appropriate measure of
ionization and neglects additional activity effects.
It is not a universal exact acid constant measurement.
Check whether the supplied quantity is conductivity or molar conductivity,
whether the units agree, and whether the concentration is in the required
units.
Use the twelve original quiz questions and seven worked examples to connect
these calculations with cells, redox balance and electrolysis.
